_comment: Patch notes for the website and releases. Maintained by etl/changelog.py; add notes for the next release under 'unreleased'.

website: Every field on the Lua export page has an ⓘ explaining what it contains and how it appears in the Lua file.
The site no longer scrolls sideways on phones: the menu wraps onto a second line and the export form fits the screen.
In the Lua export the quest fields starters and enders are now called startedBy and finishedBy, matching QuestieDB.
Italian is now in the language menu; its quest texts come from Wowhead and appear as they are imported.
The database is also online at data.morthen.net, updated after every data release.
data: Quest texts that QuestieDB, VMangos and the game cache lack can now be filled in from Wowhead in every language; quests using them list Wowhead as a source.
NPCs, objects and items that have no name in QuestieDB use the VMangos name or are shown as e.g. "NPC #214954" instead of breaking the update.

website: The docker-compose.yml of each release pulls the image from Docker Hub (derskunky/wow-quest-database); the image files attached to the release carry the same name.
The Lua export page separates data fields from localization fields, each with All/None, so you can export only the data file or only the language files.

The export page is now grouped into Selection, Data file and Localization files, starts with everything ticked, disables export when nothing is selected, and keeps both field choices in the page link.

classic: No changes to quests, NPCs, objects or items.
forever: No changes to quests, NPCs, objects or items.

commits: Point the release docker-compose.yml at the Docker Hub image
Let Claude Code draft missing patch notes in the release workflow
Separate data and localization fields on the export page

website: New pages for NPCs, items and objects: they list every entry right away, with filters (zone, reaction, rank, services, quality, type, slot, level) and sorting.
Patch notes on the start page, describing the changes of each version.
Quest pages show the map ID (uiMapId) of the quest's zone, and the Lua export includes it.
New logo and favicon; the Docker Compose file of each release carries the app icon for ZimaOS.
dataNotes: Quest texts for new Forever quests on Zephras Isle, read from the game client's quest cache: 11 quests in English, 10 in German.
Every quest with a zone now has a map ID (uiMapId) for the in-game map API: 3,246 of 3,261 in Classic Era and 3,592 of 3,757 in WoW Forever.

classic: No changes to quests, NPCs, objects or items.
forever: 11 quests updated (texts, objectives, rewards or chains), e.g. Blood for Blood, Breaking the Breaker, Disrupting Logistics, Feathers for Binding, Tears of the Lady, Unwanted and Unworthy, Unwelcome Spirits, WANTED: Vulgara the Insatiable.

Release images can also be published to a private Docker Hub repository.

website: First version of the WoW Quest Database for Classic Era and WoW Forever: quests, NPCs, objects and items with detail pages, a quest list with filters and a global search.
Quest pages show objectives, descriptions, rewards and quest chains, with an interactive map of quest givers, turn-ins and objective locations.
Map images from the game clients for both versions, fully explored or with fog of war.
Questlines as a graph in the style of BtWQuests, with faction and class filters and progress tracking in the browser.
Quest texts and names in ten languages.
Lua export of all data, on the website and as a command-line tool, with texts in separate files per language.
Filters are kept in the address, so going back returns to the same view.
Docker image for self-hosting, released automatically when the data changes.
dataNotes: Initial data from QuestieDB combined with the VMangos world database: 4,257 quests in Classic Era and 4,989 in WoW Forever, plus NPCs, objects and items.
The Zephras Isle storyline (Skyborne starting zone in WoW Forever) as a questline, based on warcraft.wiki.gg.
Item rewards of Forever quests taken from QuestRewards.lua.
